title: Lane X1 — PostgreSQL Product Materialization, Migration, Rebuild, Backup, and Upgrade Boundary
released_boundary: PostgresProductStateMaterializationBoundary: a PostgreSQL-backed operational state plane that transactionally materializes Repository Estate, Investigation Timeline, and publication-history projections from published canonical evidence boundaries, distinguishes logical repositories from workspace instances, supports ordered migration, deterministic rebuild, and proven backup/restore without replacing canonical evidence authority.
stated_consumer_purpose: X0 and later distribution/recovery work can render durable public-v1 product state, restore it safely after failure or migration, and avoid treating disconnected fixtures or ephemeral in-memory projections as the product database.
deferred_seams: pg_upgrade compatibility for PostgreSQL major-version upgrades (future slice)
LISTEN/NOTIFY refresh signalling for materialized view invalidation (deferred to Gridline integration)
Delivery-mode publication deployment (publication materialization is preview-only, deployment_ready always false)
Provider-cache ingestion (W1 policy artifacts consulted, compliance reserved, no live ingestion)
Incremental/differential backups (full pg_dump only, differential deferred)
Local PostgreSQL installation/management (deferred to X4 distribution integration)
Materialized view automatic refresh (REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW is manual)
GIN/JSONB indexes for path-contained queries (default btree indexes only)

completed_work: Domain materialization framework: RepositoryEstateMaterializer, TimelineMaterializer, PublicationMaterializer consuming T3.1, T4.2, T1.2 boundaries
Repository entity vs workspace instance identity model: UNIQUE(repository_hash, workspace_root_digest), proven 2 workspace instances under 1 logical repo distinct
Timeline materialization: 24-column timeline_events table, 12 indexes, 7 degradation counts, all verification/authority classifications preserved
Publication history materialization: preview receipt storage, reconstruction state with corruption detection, deployment_ready always false
Migration lifecycle: migrations 003-006 additive, transactional, idempotent, upgrade-safe from T2.1
Materialized read models: 4 materialized views (repository estate overview, workspace status, timeline summary, publication preview summary)
Backup/restore boundary: PostgresBackupService using real pg_dump/pg_restore, content-light BackupReceipt/RestoreReceipt, secrets exclusion
Rebuild behavior: clear_projection_data covers all 15 domain tables, rebuild determinism proven for all three materializers
Models: MaterializationReceipt, BackupReceipt, RestoreReceipt, MigrationUpgradeReceipt, 4 new EvidenceSourceKind values
JSON Schemas: 4 new schema files for materialization/backup/restore/migration-upgrade receipts
Tests: 30 new real-PostgreSQL tests (85 total), all passing
Audit: comprehensive X1 audit artifact with 11 documented decisions
remaining_seams: Thread-safe concurrent materialization (single transaction per materializer, no advisory locking)
DuckDB vs Postgres projection divergence (Phase 4 equivalence tests deferred)
LISTEN/NOTIFY loss on connection failure (reconnect + full refresh pattern deferred)
Postgres unavailable fail-closed behavior (configured but unreachable → PostgresUnavailableError deferred)
CoordinationStore dual-write consistency (Postgres lease writes vs events.jsonl canonical replay — coordination layer integration deferred)

sources: PostgreSQL 17 official documentation — JSON/JSONB data types and indexing
PostgreSQL 17 official documentation — Materialized Views (CREATE/REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW)
PostgreSQL 17 official documentation — Backup and Restore (pg_dump, pg_restore)
key_findings: materialized views require UNIQUE index for CONCURRENTLY refresh; used UNIQUE indexes on all 4 MVs
pg_dump custom format supports --clean --if-exists --single-transaction for atomic restore; used in PostgresBackupService
JSONB preferred over JSON for all operational storage; all provenance columns use JSONB
NOTIFY payloads limited to ~8000 bytes; projection refresh signals use projection name strings only
pg_upgrade compatibility deferred — current implementation requires pg_dump/pg_restore for major-version migration

dirty_state_before: Clean — only pre-existing untracked files (.swift-version, lane_s3 audit, lane_x2 audit, local_inference/runtime/)
dirty_state_after: X1-owned modified and created files (see files_changed and files_created). All pre-existing dirty/untracked preserved.
telemetry_and_redaction_implications: All new models and tables are content-light — SHA256 digests only, no raw file contents, paths, secrets, or credentials. Backup/restore receipts contain digests and metadata only. Materialization build receipts are content-light. No raw observability data enters PostgreSQL operational tables.
dependency_changes: None. No new packages added. Existing psycopg[c]>=3.2 remains the sole database driver. No SQLAlchemy, Alembic, asyncpg, pgvector, or SQLite introduced.
